panels.rationale: Coronal CT shows a dense calculus in the right renal mid-calyx, consistent with a component of the staghorn calculus described in the article title and in-text. The caption identifies the calculus, and the in-text links it to a staghorn calculus extending into the mid and lower pole calyces. Air foci are also present but represent emphysematous pyelonephritis, not the target disease.

in_text_mentions: e the left kidney appeared normal. Subsequent CT urography further delineated the findings, identifying a staghorn calculus within the right renal pelvis that extended to the mid and lower pole calyces (Figures 1A, 2A) resulting in hydronephrosis (Figures 1B, 2B). The dimensions of the calculus were measured at 28 x 23 mm in the renal pelvis, 14 x 13 mm in the mid-pole, and 15 x 18 mm in the lower pole, with the lower pole calculus exhibiting hyperdensity (CT value of 1200-1300 HU). Additionally, multiple air foci were observed in the upper and interpolar calyces on imaging (Figures 1B, 2, 3).
